items.title: Flatness over the center makes the strict transform a base change
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: Counts the author Lemma, two assertions: if X is flat over S at all points lying over Z then the strict transform of X is the base change X x_S S', and if a quasi-coherent F is flat over S at all points lying over Z then its strict transform is the pullback pr_X^*F (source lines 8868-8879). The proof of part (2) - which implies part (1) by definition of the strict transform of a scheme - localises to Spec(A) and Spec(B), writes the strict transform as N' = (N (x)_A A[I/a]) / a-power-torsion, and shows the a-power torsion of N (x)_A A[I/a] vanishes: at a prime not containing a the element maps to zero by construction, at a prime containing a flatness of N_q over A removes the torsion, and Algebra's local criterion makes y zero globally.
